MATHEMATICS · CONDITIONAL PROBABILITY · FREQUENCIES → BAYES' RULE

A flag is not a verdict.

Count the flagged group before deciding how much a positive signal means.

01 KEEP THE TWO POPULATIONS SEPARATE
All items
10,000
Defective
100
Sound
9,900
True flags
90
False flags
495
02 CHANGE THE DENOMINATOR TO ALL FLAGS
90 defective / 585 flagged
15.4% defective among the flags
Purple is the defective share of the flagged group, not the detector's hit rate.
Base 1%; hit 90%; false flags 5%.
FLAGGED ITEMS 585
ACTUALLY DEFECTIVE AMONG FLAGS 15.4%
Defective items in the batch
1 %

WHY THIS MATTERED

A factory flags items for inspection. A good detector can still flag many sound items when defects are rare.

Our hypothetical batch contains 10,000 items. At a 1% defect rate, 100 are defective and 9,900 are sound. Those groups are the starting denominators for the detector's rates.

One percent of 10,000 is 100. The other 9,900 are sound.

48

20%

WHY THIS MATTERED

A dye can spread without a pump or a molecule deciding to move downhill. Compare traffic in both directions.

Give every particle the same 20% crossing chance. With 48 starting on the left, expected traffic to the right is 9.6 per tick. With 12 on the right, expected traffic left is 2.4.

The decimals are averages across many repetitions. A single trial has whole particles.

Both directions remain possible. More particles starting on the left means more chances to cross right.

OpenStax Biology · Passive transport: Random molecular movement, concentration gradients and dynamic equilibrium.
OpenStax Chemistry · Diffusion: Diffusion and its dependence on a concentration difference.

Model assumptions: 60 independent particles, equal-volume well-mixed compartments and the same crossing probability in each direction per tick. Readouts are expectations across repeated trials, not measured integer counts. Dot counts show a rounded expected split while conserving 60; dots are not tracked trajectories. Ticks are model steps, not seconds. Real diffusion has spatial gradients, interactions and fluctuations.
